input: An amine absorption unit was tested at pilot scale using gas obtained from a cement kiln, the pilot unit being a test unit, smaller than a plant unit, run in order to obtain performance figures on the actual gas before any larger installation is considered. In an amine absorption unit of this kind, the solvent takes up carbon dioxide from the gas that is passed through it and gives the carbon dioxide up again on regeneration, and it is the heat required for that regeneration which the steam demand of the process represents. Over a test period of 90 days, during which the unit was operated at 11 t of carbon dioxide per day, the unit succeeded in capturing 92% of the carbon dioxide present in the treated gas, the treated gas being the kiln gas passed through the unit and the capture figure being the share of its carbon dioxide that the solvent took out over the course of the test. The steam demand was determined to be 3.4 GJ per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, a figure which states the heat taken by the process for each tonne captured and which represents the principal energy requirement of the operation. The solvent loss was found to be 1.6 kg per tonne captured, stating the solvent lost by the unit for each tonne captured, a continuing loss which has to be made up during running. Taken together, the three figures describe the test as it was run over the whole of the 90 days, on kiln gas carrying the dust load of a working kiln. It should be noted that the results are limited to the period of the test itself. Beyond 90 days, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent remains untested, and the capture, the steam demand, and the solvent loss must accordingly be regarded as established for the tested period only.
